phase3_findings.description: _rollback_conversation guards the conversation store's missing truncate_messages method but not a call to it that raises. The lookup uses getattr(store, "truncate_messages", None) and logs at ERROR when absent, but the call at line 247 is unguarded. Its only caller is the except asyncio.CancelledError handler at lines 427 to 438, so an exception from that call would travel out of the handler and replace the cancellation the bare raise at line 438 propagates, with nothing recording that the rollback did not happen. The shipped BoundedConversationStore raises only ValueError for a negative length and the caller derives baseline_messages from len(...)-or-zero, so the shipped wiring cannot reach this path; an embedder supplying its own store could.

The two new helpers annotate the agent parameter as Any (_conversation_baseline at line 498, _rollback_conversation at line 516) although the value passed is always the Agent that get_agent returns in src/sqllens/tools/_agent.py line 44. The structural requirement this change introduces, a store with a synchronous truncate seam plus a user resolver, is expressed in no type: ConversationStore in src/sqllens/agent/core/storage/base.py declares only its five asynchronous methods, so a type checker cannot see the missing-method seam or a typo in an attribute name and the only signal is the run-time getattr probe. A narrow Protocol for the two attributes would make the dependency checkable.

The stream_request docstring still says the method "Yields text chunks as they arrive". After this change the whole stream is drained inside one asyncio.to_thread call and every chunk is yielded only after the stream has completed, which the inline comment four lines below describes correctly, so the docstring and the comment contradict each other.

The added sentence that the cleanup in the finally: block "still runs on that same thread, before the exception surfaces at the await" holds for an exception raised inside the threaded body but not for the cancellation case the surrounding paragraph is about. asyncio.to_thread cannot interrupt a running worker, so a CancelledError surfaces at the await immediately while the worker's teardown runs afterwards, which is what the bolded sentence just before it asserts. Also stored as checklist FAIL VC-17.

The inline comment repeats the same ordering claim, that "teardown runs on the thread that owns the connection, before any exception surfaces at the await". The thread-affinity half is correct; the ordering half is wrong under cancellation, where the await raises first and this finally block can run much later. The MySQL and Postgres runners carry no equivalent sentence.

The truncate_messages docstring lists three reasons for returning False and tells the reader this is "never an error". The user-mismatch case does not fit: the conversation still exists and still holds the cancelled call's messages, a failed rollback with the same consequence the sibling missing-method branch logs at ERROR. src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py lines 255 to 256 restate the claim and omit the same case, so the INFO log cannot be told apart from the harmless outcomes.

The sentence promises that "its health check keeps answering", but /healthz exists only in the HTTP transport's path normalizer, and the surrounding paragraph walks the reader through the stdio setup as well, the recommended Claude Desktop path two sentences earlier. The acceptance criterion asks only for the half saying a waiting question does not stop the server from accepting other requests; the unqualified health-check clause leads a stdio reader to expect an endpoint that is not there.
The added paragraph links to cleanup-error-handling.md twice in consecutive sentences. Both statements are true; the repeated link makes the paragraph read as though two different pages were meant.

_FakeStream.text_stream blocks on release.wait() inside the property getter, so the streaming liveness test pins that the event loop stays responsive while the stream object is obtained rather than while chunks are iterated. The real SDK blocks between chunks, inside the for loop. The test still fails against a tree without this change, so coverage of the first criterion holds; the fake is less faithful than the non-streaming and runner fakes, which block inside create and execute.

The new truncate_messages takes a raw user_id: str and compares conversation.user.id != user_id, while the sibling methods get_conversation, delete_conversation and list_conversations at lines 63 to 91 all take a User and unwrap the identity themselves. The one method that can delete data is the one whose caller is trusted to have already unwrapped it, so an unrelated string, including the empty string the caller initializes baseline_user_id to, is a well-typed argument that quietly matches no conversation and returns False, a skipped rollback. The length < 0 precondition is raised explicitly while this identity precondition is not.

## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (one Important finding and eleven suggestions, all below the critical threshold, plus one inconclusive checklist item)

This pull request is ready to merge: every one of the eleven decided acceptance criteria is implemented and pinned by a test, the reviewers found no Critical defect, and the one Important finding describes a failure path that the shipped wiring cannot currently reach.

Rule applied: rule 6 — a finding or checklist item below the threshold remains, so the verdict is APPROVE with notes.

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. In `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` (lines 235 to 247), the cancellation rollback guards the conversation store's missing `truncate_messages` method but not a call to it that raises. The method lookup uses `getattr(store, "truncate_messages", None)` and logs at ERROR when the method is absent, but the call itself at line 247 is unguarded. Because the only caller is the `except asyncio.CancelledError` handler at lines 427 to 438, an exception from that call would travel out of the handler and replace the cancellation that the bare `raise` at line 438 is there to propagate, and nothing would record that the rollback did not happen. The shipped `BoundedConversationStore` raises only `ValueError` for a negative `length`, and the caller derives `baseline_messages` from `len(...)`-or-zero, so the shipped wiring cannot reach this path; an embedder supplying its own store could. (raised by 1/4 agents)

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (11)

The two new helpers in `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` annotate the agent parameter as `Any` (`_conversation_baseline` at line 498 and `_rollback_conversation` at line 516), although the value passed is always the `Agent` that `get_agent` returns in `src/sqllens/tools/_agent.py` line 44. The structural requirement this change introduces — a store with a synchronous truncate seam plus a user resolver — is therefore expressed in no type: `ConversationStore` in `src/sqllens/agent/core/storage/base.py` declares only its five asynchronous methods, so a type checker cannot see either the missing-method seam or a typo in an attribute name, and the only signal is the run-time `getattr` probe. A narrow `Protocol` for the two attributes would make the dependency checkable. (raised by 2/4 agents)

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] While a `query_database` call is blocked inside a synchronous Anthropic client call or inside a synchronous database driver call (connect, execute or fetch), the event loop keeps running other tasks, and the HTTP transport answers `GET /healthz`. This holds for non-streaming and streaming Anthropic requests and for each of the Postgres, MySQL and SQLite runners.
- [ ] Two `query_database` calls with different conversation ids, each blocked inside a synchronous Anthropic or database call, are blocked at the same time: neither waits for the other call to finish before entering its own blocking call.
- [ ] Two `query_database` calls with the same conversation id do not overlap: the second call's agent run starts only after the first call has returned, failed or been cancelled. When both calls return or fail, the conversation's history afterwards holds the first call's messages followed by the second call's messages.
- [ ] After every call on a conversation has returned, failed or been cancelled — including a call cancelled while it was waiting for its turn — the server holds no per-conversation queue entry for that conversation id.
- [ ] When a `query_database` call is cancelled while it is running, the conversation holds none of the messages that call added and keeps every message that was in it when the cancelled call's turn began (after any earlier call on that conversation id finished). The next call on that conversation id runs with that history.
- [ ] When a `query_database` call is cancelled, the tool function raises the cancellation and returns no result.
- [ ] For the same conversation id, the same sequence of Anthropic responses and the same query results, a `query_database` call returns the same text content and the same `_meta` as before this change, apart from the duration values in the agent trace. This holds for both streaming and non-streaming Anthropic requests.
- [ ] An Anthropic API error raised during a call still produces an `isError: true` result, and a database error or statement timeout raised by a runner still produces a failed `run_sql` step that the agent can re-plan from, as before this change.
- [ ] A database query run under a profile whose `max_rows` is lower than the base config's fetches at most that profile's `max_rows` plus one rows from the driver.
- [ ] The change leaves these as they are: - It adds no interruption of work already running on a worker thread. A cancelled call's database query keeps running until it finishes or the engine's statement timeout stops it. Nothing but the query's own end stops it when `statement_timeout_ms = 0`, or when it is a MySQL statement other than `SELECT`, which MySQL's `MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` does not cover. A cancelled call's Anthropic request keeps running, and is billed, until it returns. Server shutdown waits for such threads. - It adds no thread pool of its own. Anthropic calls and database queries share asyncio's default executor, so beyond its thread count further calls wait for a free thread. The ChromaDB memory store keeps its own two-thread pool. - It leaves the synchronous memory-store calls of `import_memory` and the memory-administration MCP tools on the event loop, so those tools still block it while they run. - It leaves the scratch CSV write after each query, `df.to_csv`, and the read-only and row-level-security guards' SQL parsing on the event loop. - It adds no progress notifications and no acknowledge-now / fetch-later job API. A `query_database` call still holds its request open until the agent run ends, so a question that takes longer than a client's timeout still times out for that client.
- [ ] After the change: - `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md` states that `query_database`'s Anthropic calls and database queries run on worker threads, that calls sharing a conversation id run one at a time, that a cancelled call's messages are removed from its conversation, and that `import_memory` and the memory-administration tools still block the event loop. - `docs/internal/database-connectors/cleanup-error-handling.md` and `docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md` state that a cancelled request's database query keeps running on its worker thread until it finishes or the engine's statement timeout stops it. - `docs/external/getting-started.md` states that a question waiting on the AI service or the database does not stop the server from accepting other requests, and that `import_memory` and the memory-administration tools can still briefly block them.

checklist.source_excerpt: Server shutdown waits for such threads rather than killing them: uvicorn runs the server through `asyncio.run` / `asyncio.Runner` (`uvicorn/_compat.py`), which calls `loop.shutdown_default_executor()` on the way out. How long it waits depends on the interpreter — on Python 3.11 that call takes no timeout and waits indefinitely; on 3.12+ `asyncio.run` passes it a five-minute cap. Either way a long query can delay shutdown. The cleanup in the `finally:` above still runs on that same thread, before the exception surfaces at the `await`.

But the final sentence at cleanup-error-handling.md:41 ('cleanup in the finally: still runs on that same thread, before the exception surfaces at the await') is wrong in the very scenario the paragraph discusses: a cancelled request. With asyncio.to_thread, cancelling the awaiting task raises CancelledError at the await immediately while the worker thread keeps running the query; the thread's finally runs only later, when the query ends. The paragraph itself says the query keeps running after cancellation, contradicting the ordering claim. The absolute wording ('before the exception surfaces') breaks on cancellation.
